title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): this is the section 'Localisation pour les variétés abéliennes'. A is a commutative ring and S = Spec A. C is an A-linear category, not necessarily additive. For an A-algebra A', the category C_{A'} has the same objects as C and Hom_{C_{A'}}(X,Y) = Hom_C(X,Y) ⊗_A A'. This defines a fibred category over affine S-schemes. Grothendieck observes it is almost never a stack on the big site. When its restriction to the small Zariski site of affine opens of S is a Zariski stack, written C̲, he calls C 'localisable sur A'.

Intended application: C is the category of abelian varieties, with A = Z. Then C_{Z[1/f]} is the category of abelian varieties up to isogenies of degree invertible away from f. 'Localisable' amounts to a local-global gluing of objects along isogenies of coprime degree.

This page continues the consequences.

(b) C additive, R an A-algebra acting on X, with R → End_C(X) bijective. For P a right R-module that is locally (on S) free of finite type, P ⊗_R X exists. The functor P ↦ P ⊗_R X is fully faithful, and its essential image is the set of objects X' locally on S isomorphic to some X^n.

NB: the same conclusion holds without localisability if C is karoubian (closed under direct summands) and P ranges over finitely generated projective R-modules. This is the standard equivalence add(X) ≃ proj(End X) given by Hom(X,−).

(c) Mod(R,C) is the category of objects of C with an A-linear R-action. It is again A-linear. Grothendieck claims the fibred category A' ↦ Mod(R,C)_{A'} is equivalent to the fibred category of sections of C̲ with an R-action. On the small affine Zariski site it is therefore identified with Mod(R,C̲), which is a stack if C̲ is. Hence Mod(R,C) is localisable over S when C is.

NB: for R commutative, Mod(R,C) is R-linear. He explicitly warns that the argument does NOT prove localisability over Spec R, which would be stronger than over Spec A.

(d) Localisability is inherited by restriction to an affine open U = Spec A' of S. C_{A'} is localisable over A', and its associated stack is C̲|_U.

(e) Two objects are 'apparentés' (A-apparentés) if they are locally isomorphic over Spec A. In the abelian-variety case this is the classical notion of being in the same genus: ℓ-locally isomorphic for all ℓ, via isogenies of degree prime to ℓ. The full subcategory of objects apparentés to a given object is A-linear and localisable. Grothendieck calls it a 'catégorie de Deuring'; the definition presumably follows on the next page.

Purpose: an abstract, stack-theoretic framework for 'Deuring/Serre-tensor' correspondences. A genus of objects (e.g. abelian varieties in a genus inside an isogeny class) is to be classified by locally free rank-one modules over R = End(X), and objects locally isomorphic to powers X^n by locally free R-modules of finite type. This generalises Deuring's correspondence between supersingular elliptic curves and ideal classes of a maximal quaternion order.
errors: Slip in the text: 'la catégorie des objets de R munis d'une opération R-linéaire' should read 'objets de C'. The notation also alternates between Mod(R,C) and Mod(C,R).

In (c), A' was first restricted to affine opens of S (struck out) and then replaced by 'une A-algèbre'. For a general A-algebra, 'sections of C̲' over Spec A' is undefined, since C̲ lives only on the small Zariski site, and the equivalence fails in general.

Even for Zariski localisations A_f, the claim needs some care. Full faithfulness, Hom_R(X,Y) ⊗ A_f = Hom_{R⊗A_f}(X,Y), uses flatness plus finiteness (R finitely generated, or Hom finite). Essential surjectivity (an R⊗A_f-action on X in C_{A_f} comes from a genuine R-object of C up to isomorphism) is not argued. It holds for abelian varieties by a lattice argument but not obviously in general.
(b) as stated on the previous page omits 'bijectif' in 'si R→End_C(X)'. The intended hypothesis is clear from (a).
(e) asserts without proof that a genus subcategory is localisable. Full subcategories closed under local isomorphism do inherit the stack property, so this is fine but stated quickly.

ideas.what: A-linear category whose Hom-base-change C_{A'} forms a Zariski stack on the small affine site of Spec A ('localisable sur A')
ideas.modern_name: Linear category as a sheaf/stack of linear categories over Spec A; local-global principle for Hom-lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard name; close to lattice/genus theory (Eichler, Fröhlich) and categories linear over a base scheme

ideas.what: P ↦ P⊗_R X fully faithful from locally free (rank 1, or finite type) R-modules, with essential image the objects locally isomorphic to X (resp. to some X^n)
ideas.modern_name: Serre tensor construction / Morita-type equivalence; for abelian varieties, the 'genus ↔ locally free End-modules' correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941) for supersingular curves; Serre (tensor construction); Waterhouse (1969); Kani; Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate (2018) for powers of elliptic curves

ideas.what: Karoubian variant: add(X) ≃ projective finite-type End(X)-modules
Mod(R,C) of R-objects inherits localisability over A; explicit caveat that localisability over Spec R (R commutative) is NOT obtained
ideas.modern_name: Stability of local-global property under module objects; localisation over the centre

ideas.what: 'Apparentés' objects (locally isomorphic over Spec A) and the 'catégorie de Deuring' of a genus
ideas.modern_name: Genus of an abelian variety / lattice; class set of an order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eichler (lattices), Deuring, Waterhouse (genus in isogeny classes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an abstract categorical framework: an A-linear category localisable as a Zariski stack over Spec A. Within it, the Deuring correspondence, the Serre tensor construction and genus theory of abelian varieties all become one Morita/descent statement. The essential image of P↦P⊗_R X over locally free R-modules is exactly the objects locally isomorphic to powers of X. This anticipates, in axiomatic form, the module-theoretic classifications later proved case by case (Waterhouse 1969, Kani, JKPRST 2018).
missed.quote: son image essentielle est formée des objets X' de C qui sont localement sur S isomorphes à un objet de la forme X^n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Current work on abelian varieties isogenous to powers of a curve, class sets and mass formulas, and isogeny-graph cryptography reproves such equivalences ad hoc. A uniform 'localisable linear category' formalism, with its explicit caveat about localising over Spec End rather than Spec Z, is not standard in that literature.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open whether Mod(R,C) (R commutative) is localisable over Spec R rather than just Spec A. For abelian varieties with commutative endomorphism algebra this is a finer local-global principle at primes of the order R.
missed.quote: Notre raisonnement ne prouve pas que Mod(R,C) est localisable sur R i.e. sur Spec(R)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the question of whether genus and class-set theory works prime-by-prime over the endomorphism order (including non-maximal orders). That is relevant to Picard groups of orders versus isomorphism classes in an isogeny class.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual results are classical or routine: Morita/add(X), Deuring correspondence, Serre tensor construction, genus. The notable part is the unpublished axiomatic stack-theoretic packaging ('localisable', 'apparentés', 'catégorie de Deuring') for abelian varieties around 1965. It shows Grothendieck treating genus theory via Zariski stacks of linear categories over Spec Z, which is not in the published record.
